answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 107 answers need 107 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the relic index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the trellis audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the kernel identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 107 runs and collects one. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
